title: Other guidelines, ClinPGx and what implementation still needs

segs.text: Section twenty six. Other guidelines, Clin P G x, and what implementation still needs. C P I C, the Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium, has American authors, but three other countries publish English language guidelines. The Netherlands: the Dutch Pharmacogenetics Working Group, D P W G. Canada: the Canadian Pharmacogenomics Network for Drug Safety, C P N D S. France: the French National Network of Pharmacogenetics, R N P G x, where the R stands for the French word Réseau.

Their methods are similar and their recommendations often quite similar, because they draw on the same published science. What differs is the objective. C P I C and D P W G both focus on pharmacotherapeutic recommendations for drug and gene or phenotype combinations, but C P I C is about how available results should be used, not whether to test, while D P W G also recommends genetic testing. C P N D S recommends genetic testing. R N P G x recommends testing and names the clinical settings or conditions in which to genotype.

All four are listed side by side on the guideline annotations page of Clin P G x: for each drug, the C P I C guidance, then the Dutch, Canadian and French. They are not on the F D A tables or in the drug label.

Clin P G x is the new name of Pharm G K B. It combines three projects: the N I H funded Pharm G K B, C P I C, and Pharm Cat. So the old name is Pharm G K B, not Pharm Cat and not D P W G. It catalogs, curates, integrates and disseminates pharmacogenomic knowledge, advances clinical implementation, supports integration with genomic medicine, and promotes pharmacogenomic education.

The challenges for enhanced implementation are five needs: educate providers, educate patients, expand genetic tests to more markers, build decision support systems, and put pharmacogenomic data into the electronic health record. Pharmacists at Saint Jude's in Memphis were the first to push their hospital to put pharmacogenomic results into the records of pediatric oncology patients; even in large systems, a genotype result may be missing from the record or buried in lab reports. A decision support system gives steps to follow when genetic information is available; she said it means things like the C P I C warfarin dosing algorithm.
